descriptionPlain:
Spotify Technology is our business-to-business software team, helping organizations improve how they build and deliver software. Our products, including Backstage Portal, Confidence, and Xirp, support developers and AI-powered systems as they navigate increasingly complex engineering environments.
As an Account Executive on our Commercial team, you will drive new business for Spotify Technology. You'll focus on companies with fewer than 1,000 employees, where sales cycles typically run from weeks to a few months and success depends on a repeatable, scalable sales motion. lists.content:
• Identify and pursue new business opportunities with companies of fewer than 1,000 employees. While significant inbound demand supports the pipeline, top performers will exceed targets by treating this as a “Hunter” role in addition to converting inbound demand.

• Own the full sales cycle, from prospecting and discovery through demos, proposals, negotiations, and close.

• Manage a high-velocity pipeline across multiple opportunities, keeping deals moving with clear next steps and maintaining accurate pipeline and forecast data in the CRM.

• Achieve and exceed quarterly and annual revenue targets.

• Run efficient, repeatable sales processes and contribute to playbooks that help scale our commercial sales motion.

• Partner with Marketing on inbound and outbound pipeline generation, responding quickly to leads and identifying new opportunities.

• Articulate how Backstage Portal and Confidence solve developer experience challenges, including how AI is reshaping software development.

• Tell a compelling story about Spotify's internal approach to solving engineering challenges and how our products are proven internally at scale.

• Present case studies and customer success stories that demonstrate the impact and business value of our products.

• Partner with Sales Engineering on technical evaluations and ensure a smooth handoff to Customer Success to support onboarding, retention, and expansion.

• Share customer feedback with Product and internal teams to help shape the roadmap.

• You have 4+ years of experience in a quota-carrying sales role, including 2+ years in a revenue-closing role, ideally in SaaS, developer platforms, or cloud services.

• You have a proven track record of achieving and exceeding targets in a fast-paced, high-volume B2B environment, ideally selling to small and medium-sized businesses (SMB) or mid-market companies.

• You are skilled at managing fast sales cycles efficiently while maintaining a thoughtful and effective discovery process.

• You bring strong judgment when working with incomplete information, allowing you to prioritize high-potential opportunities and confidently move away from poorly qualified deals.

• You have experience selling to technical stakeholders, including CTOs, engineering leaders, developers, or DevOps teams.

• You are familiar with software development, Product Management, DevOps tools, or developer ecosystems.

• You can clearly communicate technical benefits and business value to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• You bring strong communication, presentation, negotiation, and closing skills.

• You are highly organized and disciplined in pipeline management, forecasting, and CRM hygiene.

• You are excited to help build a scalable sales motion with AI and enjoy working with innovative products in an evolving technology landscape.

This role is based in New York City

We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

You'll collaborate with Sales Engineering, Marketing, Product, and Customer Success to close new business, expand existing customer relationships, and cross-sell products across our portfolio. Your ability to understand both the technical depth of our products and the strategic priorities of senior engineering and business leaders will be key to your success.

Success in this role comes from long-term strategy: building account plans, developing deep relationships, and positioning our products as a strategic investment in how large engineering organizations work.

You'll collaborate with Sales Engineering, Marketing, Product, and Customer Success to close new business, expand existing customer relationships, and cross-sell products across our portfolio. Your ability to understand both the technical depth of our products and the strategic priorities of senior engineering and business leaders will be key to your success.

lists.content:
• Identify and pursue new business opportunities with organizations of 1,000+ employees. This is a “Hunter” role with significant inbound and SDR support.

• Research and prospect into target accounts, building strategic account plans that map stakeholders, priorities, and opportunities for long-term growth.

• Lead complex enterprise sales cycles, proactively engaging multiple stakeholders, including CTOs, VPs of Engineering, Product leaders, platform teams, developer experience leaders, procurement, security, and legal.

• Build multi-threaded relationships across each account and develop multiple internal champions to secure new deals and support expansion over time.

• Achieve and exceed revenue targets while maintaining accurate pipeline and forecast data for long-cycle deals.

• Structure and negotiate agreements that support customer adoption, expansion, and long-term success.

• Articulate how Backstage Portal and Confidence solve developer experience challenges at scale, including how AI is reshaping software development in large organizations.

• Tell a compelling story about Spotify's internal approach to solving engineering challenges and how our products are proven internally at scale.

• Build business cases and return-on-investment (ROI) narratives that resonate with executive buyers.

• Partner closely with Sales Engineering on technical evaluations, proofs of concept, and integration planning.

• Collaborate with Customer Success to support retention and identify expansion opportunities across business units, while sharing customer feedback with Product and internal teams to help shape the roadmap.

• Travel up to 30% of the time to meet existing and prospective customers in your regional market, strengthen relationships, and support business growth.

• You have 5+ years of experience in a quota-carrying sales role, including experience selling enterprise software, ideally in SaaS, developer platforms, or cloud services.

• You have a proven track record of closing large, complex enterprise deals and achieving or exceeding revenue targets.

• You are experienced in strategic account planning, building multi-threaded relationships, and navigating long sales cycles with multiple stakeholders.

• You have experience selling to technical and executive stakeholders, such as CTOs, VPs of Engineering, platform teams, and DevOps leaders.

• You are familiar with software development, DevOps tools, or developer ecosystems, and understand how engineering organizations make buying decisions.

• You are comfortable managing procurement processes, security reviews, and legal negotiations for multi-year agreements.

• You can translate technical value into business outcomes and communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• You bring strong communication, presentation, negotiation, and closing skills, along with a strategic approach to long-term account development.

• You are excited to help build a scalable sales motion with AI and enjoy working with innovative products in an evolving technology landscape.

We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best!

For this role, you can be within the North Americas region as long as we have a work location.
This team operates within the Eastern Standard time zone for collaboration.

Spotify transformed music listening forever when we launched in 2008. description: Our Global Content Accounting Operations team makes sure the songwriters behind the music on Spotify are accurately accounted for and paid, everywhere in the world. Reporting to the Manager of Content Accounting, you’ll support songwriter royalty accounting globally and partner closely with Legal, Licensing, Technical Accounting, and Engineering. You’ll also help shape what comes next: rolling out claiming processes in new territories as Spotify expands, finding new ways to show the accounting impact of business decisions, steering updates to our claiming systems, and streamlining month-end close in a fast-growing region.

lists.content:
• Execute the monthly global content accounting close, delivering accurate results on time for reporting, including account reconciliations, roll-forward analyses, and insight-driven flux commentary.
  • Review licensor claim files and invoices promptly and accurately, meeting all contractual deadlines and flagging discrepancies for resolution.
  • Review and interpret legal agreements to ensure royalty payments are calculated and disbursed correctly, and give clear, timely feedback to internal and external stakeholders on royalty calculations and invoice reviews.
  • Develop and refine content accounting processes and procedures, and support internal, external, and third-party audit and SOX requirements for your areas of responsibility.
  • Partner with Technical Accounting, Finance, Legal, Content, Sales, Sales Operations, FP&A, Billing, AR, IT, Tax, and business owners on policies, processes, and programs, helping drive key system initiatives and improvements.
  • Mentor, teach, and review the work of supporting members of the global accounting team, and help our offshore team with questions on invoicing and claims.
  • Take part in special projects such as ERP implementation, system enhancements, third-party audits, and ad hoc analyses.
  • Travel occasionally and be available for late nights, weekends, or holidays when the close or business needs require it.

• You hold a Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, ideally with a CPA or CA, and have 3+ years of professional experience, with Big 4 or entertainment and media experience a plus.
  • You have exceptional time management and organizational skills, with a track record of prioritizing multiple concurrent responsibilities and consistently meeting deadlines.
  • You take a proactive approach to problem-solving and continuous process improvement.
  • You’re curious about AI tools and have hands-on experience using them to drive process improvements, automations, and efficiencies.
  • You have advanced Excel skills, experience with ERP systems such as NetSuite, Oracle, or SAP, and proficiency in SQL and BigQuery.
  • You thrive in a fast-paced, constantly changing environment, and experience with IFRS and/or SOX is an advantage.
  • You communicate clearly and know how to escalate potential issues to the right team early to prevent process delays.

This role is based in New York.
 
We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home. We ask that you come in 3 times per week.

description: Royalty Operations owns the operations behind Spotify’s royalty process across music, audiobooks, lyrics, and creator content. We implement content licenses in Spotify’s proprietary royalty systems, calculate and report royalties to our rightsholder partners, provide analytics to Accounting stakeholders, and serve as the go-to team for royalty questions across the company. As our business grows more complex, we’re focused on staying accurate and on time while getting faster and more flexible through scripting, Gen AI, and agentic workflows.

lists.content:
• Build a deep understanding of Spotify’s label, publishing, lyrics, and audiobook contracts, how they’re implemented in our royalty systems, and how they flow into royalty calculations, downstream datasets, and reporting.
  • Use the team’s internal AI tooling to configure contracts in Spotify’s royalty systems and test financial outputs for accuracy before sign-off from Commercial Accounting.
  • Lead data analyses to answer royalty questions from internal teams such as Legal & Licensing and Finance, and from external partners such as rightsholders and back offices.
  • Support month-end royalty close by reviewing checks, validating calculation outputs, and escalating risks or issues.
  • Run month-end analytics, from generating the data and deck to providing commentary on fluxes, to support Content Accounting’s sign-off on final royalty figures.
  • Help build new capabilities for the team, contributing directly to how our internal AI tooling evolves as Spotify’s business grows.
  • Partner closely with Legal & Licensing, Commercial Accounting, Content Accounting, and Financial Engineering.

• You have a background in Finance, Computer Science, or a related field.
  • You have 1+ years of experience in a data analyst or technical operations role. Experience in a royalty-related role at a record label, digital service provider, or music publisher is a plus.
  • You have strong technical and data analysis skills, such as SQL, Python, BigQuery, or Google Cloud Platform.
  • You bring an AI-first approach to problem-solving and are excited to get hands-on building and evolving internal tooling.
  • You’re curious about royalties and the music industry, and how Spotify pays the people who create content on our platform. Familiarity with label, publisher, or audiobook contracts, or with DSP data files, is a bonus.
  • You’re organized and flexible, and comfortable managing multiple projects in a fast-paced environment.
  • You’re a coachable self-starter who enjoys learning new concepts and coordinating across teams to meet deadlines.
  • You’re detail-oriented with a high bar for accuracy, because our numbers drive real payouts to rightsholders.

This role is based in Stockholm.
We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home. We ask that you come in 3 times per week.

lists.content:

Develop proposals, negotiate scope and commitments with artists and labels, and coordinate delivery with teams across Spotify in Korea and globally. Set clear timelines and responsibilities for release campaigns, video and content projects, and live fan experiences
  • Help artists grow their audiences on Spotify. Guide artist and label teams on using Spotify for Artists, interpreting audience insights and applying release best practices

  • You understand how streaming and digital marketing help artists build audiences, and you can turn campaign data and market insights into practical recommendations
  • You exercise sound judgment, work independently and know when to involve others in a decision
  • You’re fluent in Korean and English, with strong written and verbal communication skills in both languages

• This role is based in Seoul
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home. We ask that you come in 3 times per week

description:
We’re looking for a leader to manage Spotify’s Music Policy team, driving our strategy and execution for many of the most important issues facing the music industry for the next decade. As our Head of Music Policy, you will lead the team shaping the rules, standards, and incentives governing Spotify’s music ecosystem, positively impacting millions of artists around the world.

The music policy team focuses on developing and implementing policies that further our mission to provide a fair and equitable opportunity for artists, songwriters, distributors, labels, and publishers on Spotify — as well as educating the music industry about our approach. The role requires a deep understanding of the music supply chain, and will work heavily in collaboration with our tech and product teams, as well as our artist partnerships team, to build and roll out policy solutions. 

The scope of policies include how Spotify’s $11 billion+ annual royalty pool is allocated; owning policy programs like Verified by Spotify, AI Persona labeling, AI Credits, and Music Spam Filter; tactics to remove incentives for bad actors and spammers; guardrails and rules for content providers around platform integrity and metadata; and strategies to future proof our platform for new trends or technologies in the music industry, like AI. In communicating these policies publicly, our focus is to educate artists and the music industry at scale, so everyone has equal access to information and resources.

In this role, you’ll work with a cross-functional team from Licensing, Marketing, Public Affairs, Product, Engineering, Trust & Safety, Music Partnerships, Music Economics, and more in leading policy initiatives for the Spotify for Artists team — from the strategy, development, and implementation of new policies, to public messaging and education, to industry advocacy and engagement.

lists.content:
• Lead a high-performing team focused on building a better future for artists, songwriters, and the music industry on Spotify.
  • Set and execute against a policy agenda for the team based on the biggest needs for artists, songwriters, music partners, listeners, and Spotify.
  • Own strategy and execution around Spotify’s music policy portfolio, including Verified by Spotify, AI Persona labeling, AI Credits, Music Spam Filter, Preferred Provider Program, and more.
  • Develop and implement new policies that equitably impact the music ecosystem on topics like royalty administration, artificial streaming, new music technologies, music platform rules, and more.
  • Partner closely with technical and operational teams on content policy — including platform integrity issues, metadata strategy, and music supply chain dynamics.
  • Work hand-in-hand with product and engineering to implement technical solutions for our policy agenda.
  • Craft clear, informative messaging about existing and new policies — and launch scaled educational initiatives to make sure artists, songwriters, distributors, and rights holders have accurate information about our platform.
  • Collaborate with Music Partnerships and Licensing to understand the needs of all the stakeholders on our music platform, to advocate for and explain new policies, and to listen to and incorporate feedback.
  • Partner with Data Science and Music Economics to deeply understand platform trends and the potential impact of various policy decisions.

• You have 10+ years of relevant experience in the music industry, policy, legal, or technology platforms.
  • You have proven experience in the music industry, working with artists and creators, and with technology platforms. You have a deep understanding of the music supply chain.
  • You’re a dedicated people leader, caring deeply about the health and growth of the people on your team.
  • You have a deep passion for technology, love getting into the weeds of technical solutions, and have experience working closely with engineering
  • You have passion for creating a more rewarding, fairer experience for artists and songwriters around the world. You love music.
  • You’re comfortable diving deep into spreadsheets, talking to technical teams, mapping out complex incentive systems, and sweating the details.
  • You’re a strong communicator and a strong listener — understanding when to influence others and when to incorporate smart feedback.
  • You’re experienced at bringing cross-functional teams together in a shared vision.

• We are a distributed workforce enabling our band members to find a work mode best for them!
  • Where in the world? For this role, it can be within the Americas region in which we have a work location
  • Prefer an office to work from home instead? Not a problem! We have plenty of options for your working preferences. Find more information about our Work From Anywhere  options here
  • Working hours? We operate within the Eastern Standard time zone for collaboration, and you will be expected to work EST hours, no matter where you are located in the Americas region.

descriptionPlain:
Spotify's Propositions team is responsible for what we offer and how we package it — the plans, tiers, and offerings that determine how hundreds of millions of people experience and pay for Spotify. As Associate Director, Proposition Strategy, you'll help shape Spotify's proposition portfolio: evaluating new opportunities, shaping packaging structures, and building the commercial case for where we invest.
This is a globally focused role for someone who thinks in business cases as much as in ideas. You'll be a commercial engine for the team, assessing the financial upside, risks, and trade-offs of each opportunity and bringing clear prioritization recommendations to senior leadership. The role is centered on strategic evaluation and decision-making rather than downstream execution or launch. You'll have broad exposure across multiple strategic priorities and work closely with partners across the business to anticipate where propositions should go next.
description:
Spotify's Propositions team is responsible for what we offer and how we package it — the plans, tiers, and offerings that determine how hundreds of millions of people experience and pay for Spotify. As Associate Director, Proposition Strategy, you'll help shape Spotify's proposition portfolio: evaluating new opportunities, shaping packaging structures, and building the commercial case for where we invest.

This is a globally focused role for someone who thinks in business cases as much as in ideas. You'll be a commercial engine for the team, assessing the financial upside, risks, and trade-offs of each opportunity and bringing clear prioritization recommendations to senior leadership. The role is centered on strategic evaluation and decision-making rather than downstream execution or launch. You'll have broad exposure across multiple strategic priorities and work closely with partners across the business to anticipate where propositions should go next.

lists.content:
• Evaluate the commercial and economic viability of new propositions — including new offerings, complementary products, and packaging structures.
  • Build robust business cases end to end, from initial hypothesis through sizing, unit economics, and scenario modelling to an executive-ready recommendation.
  • Partner closely with Finance and Licensing to validate assumptions, pressure-test models, and quantify the financial impact and licensing implications of different propositions.
  • Assess upside, risk, and trade-offs across the portfolio to drive clear prioritization decisions on which opportunities to pursue.
  • Develop a portfolio strategy that balances near- and long-term opportunities and creates more value for Spotify's listeners and business.
  • Build strong relationships across Product and other functions to understand the innovation roadmap and proactively identify commercialization opportunities.
  • Track the competitive and macro landscape to anticipate how proposition and packaging strategy should evolve over time.

• 8+ years of experience in corporate strategy, management consulting, product or monetization strategy, business development, or a similar commercial role — with a track record of turning ambiguous problems into structured, executive-ready recommendations.
  • Expert in building and owning complex financial models and business cases: unit economics, revenue and pricing analysis, scenario modelling, and cannibalization frameworks.
  • Experienced in subscription, consumer, or digital media businesses, ideally with exposure to pricing, packaging, or bundling across global markets.
  • A sound commercial decision-maker who can weigh competing opportunities, make clear prioritization calls, and defend them with data.
  • A strong communicator and trusted partner who can distill complex commercial trade-offs into crisp narratives for senior leadership and influence without authority.
  • Comfortable operating with breadth — equally at home in a spreadsheet, a cross-functional working session, and a leadership review.
  • Curious and forward-looking, with a strong point of view on how product innovation can translate into new ways to create and capture customer value.

• This role is based in New York
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

Our mission is to empower creators and consumers by delivering the best audiobook content with unmatched quality and accessibility. lists.content:
• Map the Japanese publishing and audiobook landscape and identify priority publishers, rights holders, and catalogue opportunities.
  • Build a strong pipeline of major and independent publishers, and take partnerships from first conversation through negotiation, agreement, and onboarding.
  • Lead commercial and licensing negotiations, including distribution terms and content licensing budgets, and design creative deal structures that improve economics and share risk.
  • Identify and prioritize the audiobook catalogues and titles that matter most to listeners in Japan, using data, financial models, and market insights.
  • Own long-term publisher relationships, aligning on shared goals and running regular performance reviews informed by data and partner feedback.
  • Partner with operations and publishers on catalogue onboarding, metadata readiness, and smooth content delivery, resolving issues that affect partners or listeners.
  • Represent publishing partners internally, working with product, editorial, growth, operations, and cost management teams on launch priorities and long-term improvements.
  • Stay close to developments in the Japanese publishing and audiobook market and turn them into new partnership and growth opportunities.

descriptionPlain:
The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.
We're looking for a Backend Engineer to join Babka, a team within Spotify's Data Infrastructure organization. Babka powers the analytics behind experiences like Spotify for Artists and Spotify for Creators, helping artists, creators, and music labels explore how their content performs through fast, interactive data insights.
Originally built to support music analytics, our platform now serves podcasts, audiobooks, and internal Spotify tools. As we expand our capabilities across Spotify, you'll join us at an exciting stage, with opportunities to shape our technical direction, improve our infrastructure, and make analytics easier for engineering teams to build and operate.

  • Help expand our data infrastructure platform to support new products, teams, and use cases across Spotify.

  • Build internal tools and shared services that make it easier for engineers to integrate with and use our analytics infrastructure.

  • Contribute to the reliability, performance, and scalability of our distributed systems, including monitoring, troubleshooting, and improving production services.

  • Collaborate with engineers and product teams across Spotify to understand their analytics needs and develop practical, scalable solutions.

descriptionPlain:
Every dataset at Spotify, from the data behind creator royalties to the signals powering recommendations, is registered, published and traced through systems our team builds. We're the source of truth for what data exists at Spotify, where it lives, who owns it, and how it flows from one pipeline to the next.
These systems sit on the critical path of the platform. Data teams use them every day to publish and find data, and other platform teams build on them for access, retention, governance and incident response. That means our work is judged on correctness and reliability, because every system built on top of ours is only as good as the metadata we provide.
This is a backend role focused on data management, working on the problems at the core of any large data platform: running a data catalog that stays accurate at scale, capturing lineage across batch and streaming workloads, managing schemas as they evolve, and guaranteeing that consumers only read complete data. We build on open standards like OpenLineage and Apache Iceberg, and define the internal standards for naming, storage and metadata that the rest of Spotify builds against. As the platform takes on new storage technologies and new kinds of data assets, those standards and the systems behind them have to evolve with it, and you'll help decide how.

lists.content:
• Build and Evolve Core Services: Design, build and operate the backend services and APIs behind our data catalog, lineage and publishing systems, and evolve them as the platform adopts new storage technologies and new kinds of data. Hold them to a high bar for correctness, performance and reliability.
  • Build Data Pipelines: Develop and run the batch and streaming pipelines that keep our metadata current, processing platform events and audit logs to capture how data is created and changed, and turning lineage and metadata into data products other teams build on.
  • Own Projects End to End: Turn what the teams using our platform need into technical designs, drive them through delivery and rollout, and own the results once they're in production.
  • Keep the Platform Healthy: Take part in on-call for critical services, build in observability and quality checks by default, and use automation, including AI tooling, to reduce toil for the team and our users.

• You have solid experience building and running backend services and APIs in production with Java, and you care about API design, versioning and backward compatibility.
  • You're comfortable with SQL and have worked with data pipelines or a cloud data warehouse such as BigQuery, Snowflake or Databricks. Hands-on experience with batch or streaming frameworks like Beam, Flink or Spark is a plus.
  • You have a working understanding of data engineering concepts such as orchestration, metadata management, data quality, governance and lineage.
  • You break problems down into clear, shippable steps, reasoning through tradeoffs and risks and converging on clear recommendations.
  • You own the quality of what you ship, including code written with AI assistance, and you care about operating it well after launch.
  • You are a strong communicator and collaborator who enjoys working across teams, and you're comfortable in a dynamic platform environment where many engineers depend on what you build and priorities evolve with the business.

• This role is based in Stockholm or London.
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

descriptionPlain:
LilEngine is leading the Lakehouse, a company-strategic effort to make Apache Iceberg a first-class citizen in Spotify's data ecosystem. We're building it in close collaboration with Google, on open standards, so that different kinds of data are queryable the same way and teams can bring the right engine, from BigQuery to Dataflow to Trino, to the job.
The work has two parts. Hecate enables Iceberg for the Parquet datasets that already exist across Spotify, so teams get the benefits without rewriting their data. Alongside it, we're building the foundations of a new Lakehouse architecture that lets workflows write Iceberg tables natively. We're shipping the MVP this cycle, and you'll help shape what comes next.
We also own BigQuery for all of Spotify. Thousands of engineers, data scientists and pipelines depend on it every day, which puts us on the critical path for storing, finding and querying data. We're judged on reliability, cost efficiency and how quickly we unblock users when something breaks. This backend role sits where open table formats, cloud data warehouses and processing engines meet.

lists.content:
• Build and evolve the lakehouse: Help build the foundations that let data workflows read and write Iceberg tables directly, from this cycle's MVP to a production-grade platform.
  • Drive adoption: Help migrate data pipelines from across Spotify onto the new stack, making the move as painless as possible through tooling, standards and hands-on support.
  • Own BigQuery at Spotify scale: Manage reservations and capacity, build monitoring and anti-pattern detection, and develop tooling like the BigQuery MCP server so teams can use BigQuery well.
  • Keep the platform healthy: Take part in a weekly support rotation and shared on-call. You'll debug production issues that span storage formats, catalog APIs, Kubernetes reconciliation, GCP IAM and BigQuery internals, and you'll automate away recurring toil.

• You have solid experience building and operating backend services in production with Java or Scala.
  • You're comfortable on GCP and Kubernetes. You can read kubectl output, reason about IAM and quotas, and work with CRDs and operators. You don't need deep expertise in all of these on day one.
  • You've worked with Apache Iceberg or JVM-based processing frameworks like Spark, Beam or Flink, or with a cloud data warehouse such as BigQuery, Snowflake or Databricks.
  • You think in systems and can connect the dots when a problem crosses several layers of the stack.
  • You like owning things in production, and you're motivated by seeing your systems run reliably for thousands of users.
  • You communicate clearly in writing and work well asynchronously across US and EU time zones.
  • You own the quality of what you ship, including code written with AI assistance.

This role is based in London or Stockholm.
 
We offer the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meeetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

descriptionPlain:
The Music Mission team owns Spotify's end to end proposition for music creators and the experiences they create for fans. The organization is dedicated to building tools and services to enable creation, promotion, expression, and monetization at scale.
Our team makes music videos easy for fans to discover and meaningful for artists, powered by scalable, intelligent infrastructure that grows with our catalog. We're building personalized music video playlists, sorting videos into meaningful categories, and learning which videos listeners are most likely to love, then helping that content reach the right people.
As a Backend Engineer, you'll help shape how millions of listeners experience music videos on Spotify, working alongside Data Engineers, Backend Engineers, and partners across product and design.

lists.content:
• Build and run production backend systems that improve how listeners discover and enjoy music videos.

  • Design, develop, and evolve scalable backend services and APIs that support high-traffic parts of the Spotify app.

  • Develop and maintain Java services and Scio data pipelines used by millions of listeners every day.

  • Partner with product managers and engineers to solve complex problems and create smooth, enjoyable experiences for listeners.

  • Contribute to system design, code quality, and reliable, well-run systems as part of an autonomous, cross-functional squad.

  • Explore and experiment with AI tools available at Spotify to improve how we build and ship.

• You have experience with Java or another JVM language, and familiarity with (or interest in learning) data pipeline tools like Scio, Apache Beam, or similar.

  • You've built and operated distributed, high-volume services in production, ideally on a cloud platform such as Google Cloud Platform.

  • You're comfortable with system design, data structures, and algorithms, and use data to inform how you design systems and make decisions.

  • You work directly with partners to understand their needs and turn them into scalable backend systems, APIs, and pipelines.

  • You enjoy working in teams where experimentation and iteration are part of everyday work.

  • You care about code quality, reliability, and maintainability, and take pride in shipping well-crafted work.

  • You bring a collaborative mindset and are comfortable working across team boundaries. Experience in data engineering or machine learning is a bonus, not a requirement.

• We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.
  • This team operates within the US Eastern timezone for collaboration

descriptionPlain:
At Spotify, our Subscriptions mission helps make the subscription experience seamless and reliable for millions of listeners around the world. We're building the technology that supports subscribers throughout their journey, from their first purchase to renewals, plan changes, and beyond.
We're looking for a Backend Engineer to join Rover, the team responsible for Spotify's core subscription system. Our services manage the lifecycle of every Spotify subscription, including activation, renewals, plan changes, grace periods, and cancellations.
You'll help build and improve the backend services and data systems that millions of subscribers depend on. Whether you're growing your engineering experience or looking for a new technical challenge, you'll have opportunities to learn, collaborate, and make a meaningful impact on Spotify's subscription experience.

lists.content:
• Design, build, and improve backend services that power Spotify's core subscription system.

  • Develop and deliver solutions that support subscription journeys, from activation and renewals to plan changes and cancellations.

  • Work with complex, large-scale systems to improve reliability, performance, and scalability.

  • Collaborate with engineers and teams across Spotify to solve technical challenges and deliver meaningful improvements for subscribers.

  • Contribute to technical discussions, share ideas, and help shape engineering decisions.

  • Work with large-scale data systems and pipelines, building your knowledge while contributing to their ongoing development.

  • Share feedback, learn from your colleagues, and contribute to a supportive and collaborative engineering culture.

• You have experience developing backend services using Python or Java and working with cloud platforms such as Google Cloud Platform or similar technologies.

  • You're familiar with database technologies such as PostgreSQL and interested in building reliable, scalable systems.

  • You have an understanding of data systems or pipelines, or an interest in developing your skills in this area.

  • You enjoy solving complex technical problems and finding practical ways to improve existing systems.

  • You communicate clearly and feel comfortable sharing technical ideas, contributing to discussions, and explaining your work to different audiences.

  • You take ownership of your work, seek feedback, and enjoy collaborating with others to achieve shared goals.

  • You bring curiosity, adaptability, and a willingness to learn as technologies and challenges evolve.

  • You may have worked with subscriptions, billing, payments, e-commerce, or financial systems, or you're interested in learning more about these areas.

• This role is based in London or Stockholm

  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

descriptionPlain:
Sell what you love. For us and millions of users across the globe, that’s Spotify. Join the Sales team and you’ll build the relationships that help grow our business in existing markets and beyond. We don’t just sell creative solutions to our clients and partners, we help to shape them; using our expert knowledge of ad products, sales channels and the industry to impact the way the world experiences music and podcasts. 


We are looking for an exceptional Client Partner to join our Emerging & Scaled team, one of the fastest-growing units within Spotify’s Ad Sales organization. This role is perfect for someone who wakes up every morning excited to connect with clients and inspire them with the power of Spotify. 
You bring curiosity, resilience, and a collaborative mindset, along with a passion for building meaningful client partnerships. Integrity and a healthy work-life balance are non-negotiable. You’ll shape how Spotify advertisers reach audiences and elevate their connection to our platform.
description:
Sell what you love. For us and millions of users across the globe, that’s Spotify. Join the Sales team and you’ll build the relationships that help grow our business in existing markets and beyond. We don’t just sell creative solutions to our clients and partners, we help to shape them; using our expert knowledge of ad products, sales channels and the industry to impact the way the world experiences music and podcasts. 

Sell what you love. For us - and millions of users across the globe - that’s Spotify. If you’re ready to join a team that’s passionate, innovative, and driven, then this is your opportunity to make a meaningful impact. At Spotify, our Sales team isn’t just about selling creative solutions, it’s about shaping how the world connects with music and podcasts. We use our deep expertise in ad products, sales channels, and industry trends to redefine our clients’ experience and unlock growth opportunities.

We are looking for an exceptional Client Partner to join our Emerging & Scaled team, one of the fastest-growing units within Spotify’s Ad Sales organization. This role is perfect for someone who wakes up every morning excited to connect with clients and inspire them with the power of Spotify. 

You bring curiosity, resilience, and a collaborative mindset, along with a passion for building meaningful client partnerships. Integrity and a healthy work-life balance are non-negotiable. You’ll shape how Spotify advertisers reach audiences and elevate their connection to our platform. Collaborating closely with fellow EU Client Partners and Sales leadership, you’ll grow and expand Spotify’s advertising presence with advertisers in France.

lists.content:
• Client Strategy: Lead consultative selling to inspire clients and demonstrate how Spotify can achieve their business goals.

  • Business Development: Proactively identify and cultivate high-potential customer relationships across diverse verticals to grow a robust sales pipeline.

  • Sales Propositions: Craft and present effective sales propositions, leveraging the latest platform innovations, research, and key insights.

  • Sales Targets: Own and exceed ambitious revenue goals through strategic, entrepreneurial approaches that drive sustainable growth.

  • Strategic Insight & Reporting: Deliver actionable insights and detailed performance reports, analyzing campaigns to recommend improvements.

  • Product Expertise: Stay ahead of Spotify’s product innovations, identifying cross-selling opportunities to help clients succeed.

  • Pipeline Development: Skillfully manage multiple complex conversations, prioritizing engagements with efficiency using relevant software tools.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Collaborate with Product, Marketing, and Data teams to create comprehensive strategies and optimize platform effectiveness

• Knowledgeable: You bring a minimum of 5+ years of experience managing pipelines and driving revenue in a digital advertising tech environment. Experience in audio advertising and with Agency Holding Companies (Havas, Publicis, WPP, Dentsu, OMC…) are a plus.

  • Organized & Self-Reliant: You excel in a dynamic environment, independently handling varied demands with confidence.

  • Articulate: You are an effective communicator, clearly expressing both your stakeholders’ needs and your own.

  • Intrinsically Motivated: You are driven by your own goals and always aim to beat your personal best.

  • Success and Target Driven: You thrive on exceeding targets and making a tangible impact.

  • Team-Oriented: You believe in collaborative success, eager to learn from your peers and share your expertise.

  • Fluent French and English language, spoken and written is required

• This role is based in our London office.

  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

  • We ask that you come in 2-3 times per week and are open to periodic travel across France for client meetings, events, and team collaboration.

description:
Spotify is looking for a culturally fluent, strategically sharp, and creative Communications Lead to shape and share our story across MENAT+. You’ll lead communications across the Middle East, North Africa, Türkiye, and Pakistan, helping Spotify strengthen its reputation, champion regional creators, and show up in ways that feel relevant to the audiences and communities we serve.

Reporting to the Head of Communications, SAMEA, you’ll work closely with regional leadership and Spotify’s global communications teams across consumer, corporate, policy, industry, executive, and internal communications. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who combines strategic judgment with hands-on execution and knows how to navigate culturally dynamic, fast-moving markets.

lists.content:
• Shape and execute an integrated communications strategy for MENAT+, putting regional creators, audiences, and culture at the heart of Spotify’s storytelling.
  • Be a trusted communications partner to regional leadership, providing clear counsel on business priorities, reputation, emerging issues, and high-impact moments.
  • Anticipate reputational opportunities and risks and help Spotify respond thoughtfully and effectively as cultural, media, policy, and regulatory dynamics evolve.
  • Lead creator-first and earned-first storytelling that builds fandom, discovery, and cultural relevance, finding compelling stories in emerging scenes, communities, and moments that matter locally.
  • Partner with Music, Podcasts, Product, Growth, Marketing, Public Affairs, and other teams to develop communications that support Spotify’s regional priorities.
  • Connect MENAT+ priorities and perspectives with Spotify’s global communications strategy, while translating global priorities in ways that resonate with local audiences.
  • Lead corporate, executive, internal, and B2B communications, including executive positioning, thought leadership, media engagement, and strategic messaging.
  • Lead agency relationships and budgets with creativity and discipline, developing efficient approaches that deliver high-quality, locally relevant work across a diverse geographic footprint.

• You have 10+ years of communications experience, with experience leading integrated work across consumer, corporate, reputation, and policy communications.
  • You understand the media, cultural, and creator landscape across MENA, Türkiye, Pakistan, or adjacent markets and know how to build communications strategies grounded in local context.
  • You’re a strategic thinker and adaptable storyteller who can work across earned media, executive communications, influencer engagement, and integrated channels.
  • You understand how policy, regulatory, political, cultural, and media developments can shape reputation and can turn that context into thoughtful communications advice.
  • You’re fluent in English and Arabic and/or Turkish, with the ability to communicate effectively with audiences, media, and stakeholders across the region.
  • You bring sound judgment to sensitive or fast-moving situations and can give senior leaders clear, considered advice when the stakes are high.
  • You’re comfortable working across a global, cross-functional organisation and can build alignment, share context, and influence without relying on formal authority.
  • You’re curious about music, creators, culture, technology, and the changing media landscape, and you bring a collaborative, resourceful, and hands-on approach to getting great work done.

• This role is based in Dubai
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

descriptionPlain:
At Spotify, we believe that music, podcasts, and culture move the world. We’re looking for a Content Marketing Manager to shape how Spotify shows up across Indonesia’s social platforms. You’ll help bring Spotify’s music, podcast, and cultural moments to life through storytelling that Indonesian audiences want to follow, engage with, and share.
 
Based in Jakarta and reporting to the Content & Social Marketing Lead - Indonesia, you’ll be a hands-on member of the team, turning cultural insights and marketing priorities into locally relevant content. You’ll work closely with agency partners, creators, artists, labels, and teams across Spotify to develop and deliver content across TikTok, Instagram, X, and emerging channels. You’ll combine strong creative instincts with performance insights to understand what’s working, adapt quickly, and keep Spotify relevant in fast-moving cultural conversations.

lists.content:
• Own the day-to-day execution of Spotify Indonesia’s social channels across Meta, TikTok, X, and emerging platforms, helping strengthen Spotify’s position as a go-to platform for music and podcast fans in Indonesia.

  • Contribute to Spotify’s social voice and presence in Indonesia, creating culturally relevant, platform-native storytelling that feels authentic to local audiences while remaining consistent with Spotify’s brand.

  • Lead content marketing initiatives tied to artist and podcast releases, live events, editorial moments, and on-platform campaigns, including video content from ideation through distribution.

  • Spot cultural trends, fandom signals, emerging formats, and conversations early, translating them into relevant content opportunities for Spotify.

  • Brief and collaborate with agencies and internal cross-functional teams to develop and produce content across social and other relevant media channels.

  • Build and maintain relationships with artists, labels, podcast and video creators, agencies, and internal partners, identifying opportunities for content and co-creation while managing expectations and keeping projects moving.

  • Navigate a high-volume stakeholder environment across Marketing, Creative, Editorial, artist and label partnerships, and global teams while maintaining alignment and delivering at pace.

  • Use data and performance insights to evaluate content, optimize approaches, and clearly communicate learnings and recommendations to internal partners.

  • Share learnings and best practices with regional and global teams, contributing to how Spotify approaches content and social marketing across markets.

• You have 7+ years of experience in content marketing, including social media, with experience spanning strategy and creative work in Indonesia.

  • You have a strong understanding of Indonesia’s digital and social landscape, fandom behavior, cultural conversations, and the ways audiences engage across different platforms.

  • You have experience working with creators, agencies, and cross-functional teams to deliver impactful social and content campaigns.

  • You’re confident planning and developing social media and content marketing strategies that can extend across other relevant media channels.

  • You have strong creative instincts and are deeply connected to internet culture, music, podcasts, and fandoms, with an eye for emerging trends, formats, and conversations.

  • You’re comfortable using data and insights to inform creative decisions, measure performance, and optimize campaigns.

  • You’re skilled at managing multiple stakeholders across internal teams, external partners, agencies, and creator ecosystems.

  • You’re organized and comfortable managing multiple projects and priorities in a fast-moving environment.

  • You have strong communication skills in Bahasa Indonesia and English. You’re familiar with Spotify as a product and understand how audiences use and engage with the platform.

  • Experience across broader marketing and media channels, including creator and influencer marketing, will help you thrive in this role.

• This role is based in Jakarta.

  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

descriptionPlain:
We are looking for a Data Scientist to join the Business Analytics team within Spotify’s Business Strategy and Insights organization. Our team tackles some of Spotify’s most consequential strategic questions, shaping the trajectory of our business and improving the experiences of our over 700M active users across more than 180 countries.
In this role, you will use data analysis, experimentation, and statistical modeling to identify, assess, and launch a broad range of new initiatives and product features focused on payments and payments fraud. You will also regularly assess the health of our business and identify areas of opportunity, translating these insights into clear, actionable recommendations for senior leadership.
At Spotify, you'll have access to some of the richest datasets in the world and the autonomy to explore them creatively and rigorously. Above all, your work will shape how the world listens, discovers, and connects through audio.

Our team tackles some of Spotify’s most consequential strategic questions, shaping the trajectory of our business and improving the experiences of our over 700M active users across more than 180 countries.

lists.content:
• Develop data-driven strategies to support the growth of Spotify’s active users and subscribers
  • Create and communicate impactful findings and recommendations that improve the
  • Premium product and the way we process payments
  • Model and forecast the impact of new business initiatives
  • Work closely with business partners to understand the changes they are driving and help them discover new opportunities for growth
  • Analyze experiments (A/B tests; quasi-experiments) to measure the impact of new features and go-to-market initiatives
  • Present your findings to senior leaders, influencing the course of our business

• You have 5+ years of professional experience in data science or analytics, ideally at a consumer tech company or top-tier consulting firm.
  • You are fluent in SQL and Python or R, and have a strong grasp of statistical methods and causal inference. Direct experience with product analytics, experimentation, or payments is a plus.
  • You enjoy partnering with a range of cross-functional stakeholders and working on varied projects involving different products and problem spaces.
  • You have a strategic mindset and an eye for cleanly extracting the “so what” from complex, technical analyses.
  • You are an excellent communicator adept at presenting to senior leadership and audiences of varying levels of technical knowledge.
  • You are comfortable working through ambiguous, complex problems and don’t get discouraged when the path forward isn’t immediately clear.
  • You hold at least a Bachelor’s degree in Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field.

• This role is based in London
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

descriptionPlain:
The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.
You run our websites, search, webinars and email across the Spotify Technology portfolio. Your job is to bring people into the funnel and move them through it: from finding us in search or at a webinar, to signing up, to becoming an active user, to a meeting with sales. You also own the numbers. Every week you tell the team what’s working, what isn’t and what we’re changing. You work AI-first, you know our martech stack inside out, and you use the newest features of both.
description:

Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.

You run our websites, search, webinars and email across the Spotify Technology portfolio. Your job is to bring people into the funnel and move them through it: from finding us in search or at a webinar, to signing up, to becoming an active user, to a meeting with sales. You also own the numbers. Every week you tell the team what’s working, what isn’t and what we’re changing. You work AI-first, you know our martech stack inside out, and you use the newest features of both.

lists.content:
• Website, personalization and SEO: Own performance on our marketing sites, including landing pages, forms and conversion paths. Create personalized experiences using the latest tools. Own GA4 and GTM tracking and run A/B tests to lift conversion. Implement SEO and AI search strategies and decide which pages we need to build next.

  • Email and nurture, moving people toward sales: Build nurture paths mapped to each stage from lead to opportunity with a clear next step. Segment by role, company fit and intent so engineers, platform leads and execs each get the right message. Partner with Sales and RevOps on what sales-ready looks like, keep a regular drumbeat for people who aren’t ready yet, and write the emails yourself. Success is measured by meetings booked and pipeline, not opens and clicks.

  • Webinars, getting the most out of every one: Run every webinar end to end, from platform and landing page to invites and reminders. Grow registrations and show rate with the right audience, and manage the follow ups. Turn each webinar into on-demand pages, clips, blog posts and nurture content. Report results and keep a playbook of what works.

  • Campaign operations: Own campaign naming and UTM rules.  Build and launch your own emails, workflows, segments and lists, backed by standard QA checklists. Keep lists clean and own subscription types and consent setup, including growing opted-in lists across the portfolio. Partner with Legal on consent, privacy and data sharing so every list enters HubSpot correctly and legally.

  • Reporting: Build reporting at campaign, channel and executive levels, and own the weekly scorecard. Track spend and tool costs against pipeline, decide with the team what to scale, fix or stop.

  • AI and martech: Work AI-first every day and know our stack inside out, using the newest features as they ship.  Structure our data so AI tools return correct answers. Build AI agents and automations that cut manual work, evaluate new tools on cost and impact, and be the team’s go-to person for what the tools can do.

• You have 5+ years of experience in demand gen, marketing ops or lifecycle at B2B SaaS, selling to developers or technical buyers

  • You’ve set up marketing from scratch: tracking, email, reporting, the works. You’re comfortable in fast-moving, ambiguous environments

  • You’ve built nurture programs that moved leads to sales meetings, and can show the pipeline

  • You enjoy hands-on, individual contributor work and building programs yourself

  • You’ve run webinar programs end to end

  • You’re hands-on with GA4 and GTM. You’ve set up tracking, not just read reports

  • You’ve personalized a B2B website and can show what it did for conversion

  • You’re hands-on with a modern martech stack (HubSpot or Marketo, Braze, an attribution tool, and enrichment or intent tools like Clay or Reo.dev), using recent features, not just the basics

  • You’ve built campaign and executive reporting that leadership used to make budget calls

  • You use the latest AI tools every day for analysis, content and automation, and you’re the person others ask about what’s new

  • You have SEO experience, and you know how AI search is changing it

  • You’ve set up consent and subscription management in a CRM, and worked with legal on GDPR, CAN-SPAM and partner data sharing

  • You write well, and can show emails you wrote that performed

This role is based in New York.
We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

lists.content:
• Website, personalization and SEO: Own performance on our marketing sites, including landing pages, forms and conversion paths. Create personalized experiences using the latest tools. Own GA4 and GTM tracking and run A/B tests to lift conversion. Implement SEO and AI search strategies and decide which pages we need to build next.

  • Email and nurture, moving people toward sales: Build nurture paths mapped to each stage from lead to opportunity with a clear next step. Segment by role, company fit and intent so engineers, platform leads and execs each get the right message. Partner with Sales and RevOps on what sales-ready looks like, keep a regular drumbeat for people who aren’t ready yet, and write the emails yourself. Success is measured by meetings booked and pipeline, not opens and clicks.

  • Webinars, getting the most out of every one: Run every webinar end to end, from platform and landing page to invites and reminders. Grow registrations and show rate with the right audience, and manage the follow ups. Turn each webinar into on-demand pages, clips, blog posts and nurture content. Report results and keep a playbook of what works.

  • Campaign operations: Own campaign naming and UTM rules.  Build and launch your own emails, workflows, segments and lists, backed by standard QA checklists. Keep lists clean and own subscription types and consent setup, including growing opted-in lists across the portfolio. Partner with Legal on consent, privacy and data sharing so every list enters HubSpot correctly and legally.

  • Reporting: Build reporting at campaign, channel and executive levels, and own the weekly scorecard. Track spend and tool costs against pipeline, decide with the team what to scale, fix or stop.

  • AI and martech: Work AI-first every day and know our stack inside out, using the newest features as they ship.  Structure our data so AI tools return correct answers. Build AI agents and automations that cut manual work, evaluate new tools on cost and impact, and be the team’s go-to person for what the tools can do.

• You have 5+ years of experience in demand gen, marketing ops or lifecycle at B2B SaaS, selling to developers or technical buyers

  • You’ve set up marketing from scratch: tracking, email, reporting, the works. You’re comfortable in fast-moving, ambiguous environments

  • You’ve built nurture programs that moved leads to sales meetings, and can show the pipeline

  • You enjoy hands-on, individual contributor work and building programs yourself

  • You’ve run webinar programs end to end

  • You’re hands-on with GA4 and GTM. You’ve set up tracking, not just read reports

  • You’ve personalized a B2B website and can show what it did for conversion

  • You’re hands-on with a modern martech stack (HubSpot or Marketo, Braze, an attribution tool, and enrichment or intent tools like Clay or Reo.dev), using recent features, not just the basics

  • You’ve built campaign and executive reporting that leadership used to make budget calls

  • You use the latest AI tools every day for analysis, content and automation, and you’re the person others ask about what’s new

  • You have SEO experience, and you know how AI search is changing it

  • You’ve set up consent and subscription management in a CRM, and worked with legal on GDPR, CAN-SPAM and partner data sharing

  • You write well, and can show emails you wrote that performed

This role is based in London or Stockholm.
We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

descriptionPlain:
Spotify's Emerging & Scaled (E&S) business is growing rapidly across the US and Canada, and we're investing in accelerating first-time advertiser growth. As part of our mission to help brands connect with fans through audio and video, we're expanding our New Business organization.

We're looking for an experienced Director of Sales to lead our New Business acquisition strategy across North America. In this role, you'll lead and develop a high-performing, outbound-focused sales team, driving the full sales cycle from prospecting through closing. Reporting to E&S leadership, you'll shape scalable acquisition strategies, strengthen pipeline generation, and create a results-driven sales culture through hands-on coaching and measurable performance goals. You'll play a key role in unlocking new advertiser categories and driving sustainable net-new revenue growth.

lists.content:
• Define and lead the New Business go-to-market strategy across the US and Canada, expanding Spotify's presence in new and underpenetrated advertiser categories.
  • Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing, outbound-focused sales team responsible for the full sales cycle, from prospecting and lead qualification through negotiation and closing.
  • Build scalable prospecting strategies, outreach frameworks, and repeatable sales processes that accelerate pipeline generation and first-time advertiser acquisition.
  • Foster a results-driven sales culture through hands-on coaching, clear performance expectations, measurable KPIs, and disciplined pipeline management.
  • Develop and implement sales playbooks, vertical-specific narratives, and performance storytelling that help sellers engage prospective advertisers and convert opportunities into revenue.
  • Partner with Marketing, Sales Enablement, Product, and vendor teams to strengthen competitive positioning and develop effective acquisition strategies across Spotify's audio, video, and programmatic advertising solutions.
  • Build relationships with agencies, brands, and senior decision-makers, identifying new opportunities and turning first-time advertisers into long-term partners.
  • Own net-new revenue targets, pipeline health, forecasting accuracy, and sales performance, using Salesforce and data-driven insights to identify opportunities and continuously improve results.

• You have 10+ years of experience in digital media sales or related B2B industries, including 5+ years leading, coaching, and developing high-performing sales teams.
  • You have proven experience leading high-velocity, outbound-focused B2B sales teams, ideally within digital advertising, ad tech, SaaS, martech, or performance marketing.
  • You have a strong track record of driving net-new customer acquisition, building scalable prospecting strategies, and leading teams through the full sales cycle, from initial outreach to closed-won business.
  • You know how to build a results-driven sales culture through disciplined pipeline management, measurable KPIs, hands-on coaching, and continuous performance improvement.
  • You have a deep understanding of digital advertising, including direct and programmatic buying, measurement, advertising technology, and data-driven solutions.
  • You have experience setting and delivering ambitious new-business revenue targets, using pipeline metrics, conversion data, and sales forecasting to guide decisions and improve performance.
  • You know how to build trusted relationships with senior agency and brand decision-makers, understand their business challenges, and communicate the value of advertising solutions.
  • You are an inclusive, collaborative leader who enjoys developing talent, building strong teams, and partnering across functions to achieve shared goals.

• This role is based in New York
  • We ask that you come into the New York office 2-3 times per week.
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

description:
The Music Mission team owns Spotify’s end to end proposition for music creators and the experiences they create for fans. The team is dedicated to building tools and services to enable creation, promotion, expression, and monetization at scale.

Editorial UK & Ireland sits at the heart of the listener experience on Spotify. We reflect culture and drive artist discovery through playlists, storytelling formats, and tools, with a focus on new music. As our Pop Editor, you’ll bring deep cultural expertise and a data-informed approach to shape how millions of people discover music across playlists, video, and other parts of the app.

lists.content:
• Spot music and pop culture trends across the UK and Ireland early, and turn them into programming and promotional opportunities for Spotify.
  • Curate, analyse, and maintain a large portfolio of playlists for a range of audiences, moods, and moments, identifying content gaps across genres.
  • Develop and produce editorial video series, from formats and scripts to storyboards, and appear on camera to interview artists.
  • Brief internal and external creative teams with clear direction, and manage feedback through to delivery.
  • Write titles, descriptions, social posts, and in-app copy with a strong, unbiased editorial voice.
  • Use data and analytics, including video performance, to understand listener behaviour and shape future content.
  • Lead cross-functional projects end to end with Artist & Label Partnerships, Marketing, Comms, product teams, and our global editorial team, and present results within the market.

• You have 5+ years of experience in the music industry, whether programming music for streaming, TV, radio, or other media, or working in music journalism or content.
  • You have deep knowledge of music and culture, with a focus on pop and pop culture in the UK and Ireland, and a wide understanding of genres and styles.
  • You have a track record of discovering emerging artists, songs, and trends ahead of the mainstream.
  • You’re numerate and comfortable analysing and interpreting data, and you use it to set goals.
  • You communicate ideas clearly, whether in a creative brief or a single line of copy, and you have strong organisational skills.
  • You’re comfortable working on camera and interviewing artists, or keen to learn. Presenting or video production experience is a bonus.
  • You know Spotify well as a user and fan, and you understand how it fits into the wider UK and Ireland music ecosystem.
  • You’re a great teammate who adapts well to change, cares about detail, and is open to new tools.

• You’ll be based in our London office.
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best. There will be moments that require in-person collaboration, and the team will plan for these intentionally.

descriptionPlain:
Music Expression builds the tools artists use to show who they are on Spotify and to connect with fans. A song doesn't have to be just a track in a list. On Spotify it can come with a looping Canvas visual, a music video, a vertical-video clip from the artist, or a countdown to a new release. Release day can become a shared Listening Party. Every one of those things was built by this org. Each squad owns part of the artist-to-fan journey.
The work runs from video pipelines and serving infrastructure through mobile and web clients to rights systems, so engineers get real depth and range. Product, design, data science, research and product marketing work inside the squads, and they work directly with artists and labels. What you ship changes how artists show up on Spotify and how fans experience their music. If you want to work where technology meets creativity and culture, this is the place.
If this role excites you but you don't meet every requirement, we'd still love to hear from you. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds.

Spotify's in-house creative studio, Reverb, brings our brand to life through thoughtful design, visual storytelling, and creative production. Working across brand and communications, the team creates work that connects with audiences around the world.
We're looking for a Global Creative Lead to shape the visual direction of Reverb and lead a talented team of graphic designers, motion designers, and producers. You'll combine creative vision with hands-on leadership, helping the team deliver distinctive, high-quality work while building an environment where people can collaborate, experiment, and grow.
Reporting to the Director, Global Experiential & Content Production, you'll play a key role in shaping the studio's creative output and how we work together.

You'll combine creative vision with hands-on leadership, helping the team deliver distinctive, high-quality work while building an environment where people can collaborate, experiment, and grow.

Reporting to the Director, Global Experiential & Content Production, you'll play a key role in shaping the studio's creative output and how we work together.

lists.content:
• Lead and develop a team of approximately 5–6 graphic designers, motion designers, and producers, supporting their creative growth and career development.

  • Shape the visual and motion design direction across Reverb projects, creating distinctive work that brings Spotify's brand and stories to life.

  • Partner with teams across brand, communications, marketing, and production to turn creative briefs into engaging visual experiences across channels and formats.

  • Guide creative development from concept through delivery, providing clear direction, constructive feedback, and thoughtful design decisions.

  • Manage project intake, priorities, budgets, timelines, and resources to help the team deliver meaningful work across multiple projects.

  • Collaborate with Reverb's creative and production leads to build a connected, effective studio and a consistent creative experience.

  • Present creative concepts and recommendations to senior stakeholders, explaining the thinking behind decisions and building alignment.

  • Work with internal teams and external creative partners to maintain design quality, manage production needs, and navigate relevant legal and licensing requirements.

• You bring 8+ years of experience in graphic design, visual design, or a related creative discipline, with a portfolio demonstrating strong visual storytelling, brand identity, and motion design.

  • You have 4+ years of experience leading creative teams, with a thoughtful approach to coaching, feedback, and helping others develop their craft.

  • You're comfortable shaping creative direction across digital, social, advertising, editorial, and long-form brand content, adapting your approach to different audiences and formats.

  • You have experience using Adobe Creative Cloud, Figma, and relevant visual or motion design tools, and you're curious about how emerging technologies can support the creative process.

  • You know how to balance creative ambition with practical delivery, making thoughtful decisions around timelines, budgets, and resources.

  • You communicate creative ideas clearly and enjoy collaborating with designers, producers, and partners across different disciplines and regions.

  • You have experience working with external creative studios, production companies, and partners, including managing budgets, contracts, and production workflows.

  • You care about creating an inclusive, supportive team environment where different perspectives are valued, feedback is welcomed, and people can do their best work.

• This role is based in New York City.

  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! We ask that you come into the office 1-2x per week.

Japan is Spotify's only single-country region, and we're entering an exciting new chapter focused on partnerships and sustainable growth. lists.content:
• Lead Spotify's growth strategy in Japan, driving Premium subscriber acquisition, conversion, retention and revenue performance.
  • Own and deliver the Premium growth plan, identifying opportunities across the customer journey and translating them into measurable business outcomes.
  • Work closely with Marketing, Music and Partnerships leadership to shape growth priorities based on consumer insights, market trends and competitive dynamics.
  • Partner with our Partnerships team to unlock subscriber growth through telecommunications, device, payment and content partners.
  • Design and run experiments across paid, owned and in-app channels, using data and clear success metrics to improve conversion and retention.
  • Develop CRM and lifecycle marketing strategies across email, push notifications and in-app messaging, creating relevant experiences that engage and retain listeners.
  • Collaborate with Product, Data Science, Payments and Finance teams to build business cases, evaluate performance and identify scalable growth opportunities.
  • Lead and develop a team member, share learnings with regional Growth teams and explore how AI-powered tools can improve decision-making and execution.

• You have experience driving growth in a digital consumer business, such as streaming, entertainment, e-commerce or consumer technology.
  • You have a track record of owning subscriber or commercial growth targets and understand how acquisition, conversion and retention contribute to sustainable growth.
  • You're experienced in digital marketing, CRM and lifecycle campaigns, with the ability to turn customer insights into meaningful action.
  • You're confident using data, analytics tools and experimentation to make decisions, evaluate performance and identify opportunities. Familiarity with SQL can help you go further.
  • You understand subscription business economics, including customer lifetime value, subscriber acquisition cost and gross margin.
  • You combine analytical thinking with creative marketing instincts and a strong understanding of Japanese consumer behaviour and culture.
  • You're comfortable collaborating across functions, influencing stakeholders and taking ownership of initiatives in a fast-moving environment.
  • You enjoy developing others, are curious about using AI to improve how you work, and communicate fluently in Japanese and confidently in business English.
  • Please apply to this role with your CV/Resume in English

• This role is based in Tokyo
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

Sell what you love. For us and millions of users across the globe, that’s Spotify. Join the Sales team and you’ll build the relationships that help grow our business in existing markets and beyond. We don’t just sell creative solutions to our clients and partners, we help to shape them; using our expert knowledge of ad products, sales channels and the industry to impact the way the world experiences music and podcasts.
